messages:
sandeep (Acme Corp): Hey team — we're seeing intermittent silence on streaming responses from the Redwood websocket endpoint when going through our VPC. Connection stays open, but no chunks delivered for ~30-120s, then data resumes. Started after we pushed an NGINX sidecar + corp IPS update.

maria (Redwood Support): Sorry you're hitting this, sandeep. Can you share your topology (client -> LB -> proxy -> app -> Redwood)? Any TLS termination in the middle? Also roughly when this started and a sample client timestamp would help.

sandeep (Acme Corp): Topology: client -> AWS ALB (TLS) -> NGINX sidecar (proxy_pass to private Redwood endpoint) -> NAT gateway egress. TLS is intact client->ALB and ALB->sidecar (we terminate at ALB, re-TLS to sidecar). Started after sidecar update last week.

alex (Redwood Eng): Two common culprits: (1) a middlebox (ALB/nginx/IPS) buffering because it thinks it's HTTP (waiting for content-length) and not flushing chunked frames; (2) idle timeout on a device that closes or stalls the TCP flow for websockets. Do you have the sidecar nginx config? small snippets help.

sandeep (Acme Corp): Here's the proxy snippet we rolled out:

```
location /ws/ {
  proxy_pass https://redwood-private.internal;
  proxy_http_version 1.1;
  proxy_set_header Upgrade $http_upgrade;
  proxy_set_header Connection "upgrade";
  proxy_read_timeout 60s;
}
```

We didn't touch proxy_buffering explicitly.

ingrid (Redwood SRE): That proxy_read_timeout of 60s is suspicious. If the sidecar or ALB has an idle timeout at ~60s it can kill or buffer the stream. Also many IPS boxes will buffer until they see an end-of-stream or a larger chunk. Websockets should be TCP-upgraded and not treated like buffered HTTP responses.

maria (Redwood Support): Quick repro checks we recommend:
- Run wscat/tiny websocket client directly to your sidecar and capture tcpdump on the sidecar to confirm packets leave toward Redwood vs being held.
- Curl streaming test to Redwood (from inside your VPC) to validate chunk boundaries:

```
curl -v -H "Accept: text/event-stream" --no-buffer \ 
  -H "Authorization: Bearer <token>" \
  https://redwood-private.internal/v1/stream?model=... 
```

- Check ALB idle/timeouts and switch to TCP NLB for testing (avoids HTTP buffering behavior).

sandeep (Acme Corp): We ran tcpdump and saw server packets arriving at the sidecar, but the sidecar emits nothing to the client during the silent period. Looks like nginx is sitting on buffered data.

alex (Redwood Eng): That nails it — nginx is buffering. Two quick mitigations:
1) Disable proxy buffering and ensure upstream flush:
```
proxy_buffering off;
proxy_set_header Connection ""; # let Upgrade header flow
proxy_http_version 1.1;
chunked_transfer_encoding off; # sometimes helps, but test
proxy_ignore_client_abort on;
```
2) Add explicit websocket ping/pong or short keepalive frames from the client every 15-20s so middleboxes see activity.

Also add header to tell some proxies not to buffer: `X-Accel-Buffering: no`.

sandeep (Acme Corp): We added `proxy_buffering off;` and `X-Accel-Buffering: no`, bumped `proxy_read_timeout` to 300s, and sent a test — seems much better, chunks now reach client continuously.

ingrid (Redwood SRE): Great. For a longer-term fix:
- Consider using an NLB in TCP mode to avoid ALB/HTTP buffering if you must preserve raw streams.
- Ensure corporate IPS/firewall allows long-lived TCP flows; some will silently aggregate or drop after their own idle threshold.
- If using TLS re-termination in the path, ensure the re-TLS device forwards Upgrade/Connection correctly and doesn't re-chunk responses.

maria (Redwood Support): One more note: when middleboxes do deep packet inspection (DPI) they sometimes wait for full TLS application data to make decisions — that causes exactly the "silent apauses" you saw. If you can whitelist Redwood egress IPs in your IPS or route streaming traffic through a dedicated gateway, you'll avoid DPI buffering. We can share our egress ranges. :+1:

sandeep (Acme Corp): Thanks — we'll test with IPS allowlist and NLB. If we still see issues, we'll capture a pcap and share. Appreciate the quick help.

maria (Redwood Support): Thanks, sandeep. If you can attach the pcap and a short tcpdump showing sequence/packet times we can escalate to eng-runtime for deeper kernel/socket analysis. I'll also open an internal ticket to flag streaming behavior and add notes to the Private/VPC troubleshooting doc.

support-bot: Ticket created: #SUP-4821 — assigned to eng-runtime for follow-up if pcap attached.

sandeep (Acme Corp): Will do. Leaving this thread open while we validate. Thanks! :wave:
